title: Procedures — Auxiliary Power Unit Start and Bleed Use

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: Flight crew procedure for starting the auxiliary power unit and taking bleed air from it, including the wait between availability and load acceptance and the behaviour expected at high field elevation.

sections.purpose: This entry gives the flight crew procedure for starting the auxiliary power unit and for transferring the air conditioning to it, and describes what to expect between the availability indication and load acceptance.
sections.description: The auxiliary power unit supplies electrical power and bleed air on the ground and, within its published envelope, in flight. After the start sequence completes the aeroplane displays an availability indication, which confirms that the unit is running and that electrical power may be taken. Bleed air is not available at that moment: the aeroplane holds the air load off for a short stabilisation period, and the length of that period increases with field elevation and ambient temperature. At a high elevation aerodrome on a warm day it may be several minutes before the packs can be transferred. This is the aeroplane protecting the unit and is not a fault. The crew has no indication of how long the period will be and should plan the turnaround on the assumption that it is longer at high elevation.
sections.crew_procedure: Select the auxiliary power unit master switch on and, when the availability indication appears, select the start switch as required by the electrical procedure. Take electrical power as soon as availability is indicated. For bleed air, select the auxiliary power unit bleed on and wait for the pack transfer to complete; do not cycle the bleed switch if the transfer does not complete immediately. At high elevation aerodromes allow additional time in the turnaround plan before ground air is disconnected.
sections.limitation_note: The published altitude and temperature envelope for auxiliary power unit bleed use is in the limitations section. Bleed air must not be used above the published altitude, and the ground air connection should be retained until the pack transfer has completed.

type_data.crew_action: Start, take electrical power at availability, then wait for the pack transfer before disconnecting ground air.
